topics.title: Big, bigger, biggest
topics.keywords: size sizes big bigger biggest heading headings font-size scale steps important
topics.explain: Good pages use only a few text sizes, and each size is clearly bigger than the one below it. Make each step at least 1.25 times as big: 16, 20, 25, 31, 39. Then your eyes see at once what matters most.

code.text:
My space club

Planets

Mars

Mars looks red because its dust is full of rust.

legend.means: is normal text
is 16 times 1.25
is 20 times 1.25
is two steps up, for the biggest title

insert.text:
<style>
  p { font-size: 16px; }
  h3 { font-size: 20px; }
  h2 { font-size: 25px; }
  h1 { font-size: 39px; }
</style>

topics.turn: change 25px to 21px. Now Planets and Mars look almost the same. Which one is more important?
topics.bar: change **25px** to **21px**. Now Planets and Mars look almost the same.

topics.title: Give things room
topics.keywords: space spacing room gap margin crowded squashed group groups apart
topics.explain: Things that belong together sit close. Different groups get more space between them, so a heading sits nearer its own text than the group above. Pick a few space sizes and use only those, like 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64 pixels. Each one is double the one before.

code.text:
Mars

The red planet. It has two small moons.

Saturn

It has rings made of ice and rock.

is a small space, inside a group
is a big space, between groups

topics.title: Easy to read
topics.keywords: read reading readable line-height lines long wide width ch contrast gray grey dark light
topics.explain: Very long lines make your eyes tired, so stop text at about 70 letters wide with max-width: 70ch. line-height puts air between the lines. Use dark text on a light background, or light text on a dark one. Normal text should be at least 16px.

code.text:
The Moon

The Moon has no light of its own. It shines because light from the Sun bounces off it. We always see the same side of the Moon, because it turns once each time it goes around the Earth.

legend.means: is about 70 letters wide
puts air between the lines
is almost black, easy to read on white

topics.title: Two fonts that go together
topics.keywords: font fonts font-family pair match together serif sans-serif letters typeface
topics.explain: Use one font for headings and one for reading, and never more than three in all. Pick two that look different: one with little feet on its letters (serif) and one without (sans-serif). Only fonts on your Mac work, like Futura, Georgia, Rockwell, Optima and Avenir Next. The word after the comma is a backup.

code.text:
The Dinosaur Club

The biggest ones

Some dinosaurs were longer than two buses. These giants ate only plants.

legend.means: is for headings, with a backup
is for reading, with a backup

topics.title: Choose your colors
topics.keywords: color colors colour colours palette accent theme var variable background quiet gray grey
topics.explain: Pick a few colors and give each one a job: a background, a text color, and one bright accent for what matters most. For quiet text, use a lighter shade of your main color, not gray. Name your colors in :root and use them with var(). Change one line, and the whole page changes.

code.text:
Night sky club

We look at the stars every Friday.

Bring a warm coat and a hot drink.

legend.means: names a color by its job
uses that color
is a light blue for quiet text, not gray

insert.text:
<style>
  :root {
    --background: #0b1d3a;
    --text: #f1f5ff;
    --accent: gold;
  }
  body {
    background: var(--background);
    color: var(--text);
  }
  h1 { color: var(--accent); }
</style>

topics.turn: change #9fb3d9 to gray. See how dull the quiet line looks? Then change gold to hotpink. Two things change at once.

topics.title: Shadows that look real
topics.keywords: shadow shadows box-shadow soft blur blurry depth float lift rgba
topics.explain: In real life the light comes from above, so a shadow falls a little below a thing, and its edge is soft. box-shadow takes three sizes and a color: how far right, how far down, and how blurry. Use black you can see through, made with rgba, not solid black.

topics.title: Line things up
topics.keywords: line align alignment neat tidy edge straight grid columns messy left
topics.explain: Pick one edge and start everything on it: the heading, the text and the boxes. The pink line is only here to show you the edge, so take it out when you are done. A grid keeps boxes in neat rows and columns, so they always line up.

We play every week. Come and join us!

Games on Saturday

A party in June

topics.title: Buttons that say what they do
topics.keywords: button buttons click link links hover focus focus-visible words finger tap big
topics.explain: A button says what happens when you press it: a doing word and a thing, like Book a visit or Join the club. Never just Click here. Make it at least 44 pixels tall, so a finger can hit it. Let it change when the mouse is on it, and when the keyboard reaches it.

Book a visit

Which day would you like to come?

shows a ring when the keyboard reaches it

    color: white;
    text-decoration: none;
  }
  .button:hover { background: #084f4b; }
  .button:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid orange; }
</style>

topics.title: One star per page
topics.keywords: star stand out standout important attention calm busy simple loud moving
topics.explain: If everything shouts, nobody hears anything. Give each page one star: one thing that is bigger and brighter than the rest, and keep everything else calm. Let at most one thing move by itself. Here only the star moves, and only once.

code.text:
School fair

The fair is on Saturday!

There are cakes, games and prizes.

Bring your friends and family.

legend.means: is the one thing that stands out
is the only bright color
is the only thing that moves, and only once

topics.title: Looks good on a phone
topics.keywords: phone mobile tablet window screen responsive fit auto-fit minmax repeat picture pictures max-width small
topics.explain: A phone is narrow and a computer is wide, so let your page bend. repeat(auto-fit, minmax(150px, 1fr)) makes as many columns as fit, each at least 150 pixels wide. max-width: 100% stops a picture from getting wider than its box. Press the Phone button, the little phone above the page, to try it.

code.text: My pictures

legend.means: makes as many columns as fit
keeps each column at least 150 pixels wide
keeps a picture inside its box

insert.text:
<style>
  .gallery {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(150px, 1fr));
    gap: 12px;
  }
  img {
    max-width: 100%;
    height: auto;
  }
</style>
